newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Zhenye posts steep earnings rise for 96.
newsitem.headline: Zhenye posts steep earnings rise for 96.

text.p: Property developer Shenzhen Zhenye Co Ltd said on Monday it posted a 55.09 percent rise in net earnings in 1996 due to strong real estate sales.

The company said it chalked up net profits of 70.32 million yuan in 1996 compared with 45.34 million yuan a year earlier. Per-share net rose 55.39 percent year-on-year to 0.519 yuan from 0.334 yuan in 1995, the firm said in an annual report in Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Earnings surged on the back of a 68.22 percent gain in its main operating income, which soared to 185.22 million yuan from 110.11 million yuan in 1995, the company said.
Zhenye said it planned to distribute four bonus shares and a cash payout of one yuan for every 10 shares held for 1996, adding the proposal needed the approval of its shareholders.
In December, Zhenye said its shareholders had approved a plan to make a three-for-10 rights offer tentatively priced between eight and 12 yuan per rights share.
It had said it aimed to launch the offer within six months and use the proceeds in a 600-million-yuan property construction project and the acquisition of two state property firms in 1997.
It said the rights plan was being reviewed by the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
Zhenye's share capital totalled 135.62 million shares at the end of 1996, unchanged from 1995.
